title: Why you will fail to have a great career
speaker: Larry Smith

sentences.en: Transcriber: Camille Martínez Reviewer: Lalla Khadija Tigha Thank you.
sentences.zh: 抄写员：卡米尔·马丁内斯 审稿人：Lalla Khadija Tigha 谢谢。

sentences.en: I want to discuss with you this afternoon why you're going to fail to have a great career.
sentences.zh: 今天下午我想和你讨论为什么你无法拥有伟大的职业生涯。

sentences.en: (Laughter) I'm an economist. I do dismal.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 我是一名经济学家。我确实惨淡。

sentences.en: End of the day, it's ready for dismal remarks.
sentences.zh: 一天结束时，人们已经准备好发表悲观言论了。

sentences.en: I only want to talk to those of you who want a great career.
sentences.zh: 我只想和那些想要伟大事业的人交谈。

sentences.en: I know some of you have already decided you want a good career.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们中的一些人已经决定想要一份好的职业。

sentences.en: You're going to fail, too. (Laughter) Because -- goodness, you're all cheery about failing.
sentences.zh: 你也会失败。 （笑声）因为——天哪，你们都对失败感到高兴。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Canadian group, undoubtedly. (Laughter) Those trying to have good careers are going to fail, because, really, good jobs are now disappearing.
sentences.zh: （笑声）毫无疑问是加拿大团体。 （笑声）那些试图拥有好的职业的人将会失败，因为，实际上，好的工作现在正在消失。

sentences.en: There are great jobs and great careers, and then there are the high-workload, high-stress, bloodsucking, soul-destroying kinds of jobs, and practically nothing in-between.
sentences.zh: 有伟大的工作和伟大的事业，也有高工作量、高压力、吸血、毁灭灵魂的工作，几乎没有介于两者之间的工作。

sentences.en: So people looking for good jobs are going to fail.
sentences.zh: 因此，寻找好工作的人将会失败。

sentences.en: I want to talk about those looking for great jobs, great careers, and why you're going to fail.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈那些寻找伟大工作、伟大事业的人，以及为什么你会失败。

sentences.en: First reason is that no matter how many times people tell you, "If you want a great career, you have to pursue your passion, you have to pursue your dreams, you have to pursue
sentences.zh: 第一个原因是，无论人们告诉你多少次，“如果你想要一份伟大的事业，你必须追求你的激情，你必须追求你的梦想，你必须追求

sentences.en: the greatest fascination in your life," you hear it again and again, and then you decide not to do it.
sentences.zh: 你生命中最大的魅力”，你一遍又一遍地听到这句话，然后你决定不这样做。

sentences.en: It doesn't matter how many times you download Steven J.'s Stanford commencement address, you still look at it and decide not to do it.
sentences.zh: 无论您下载史蒂文·J. 的斯坦福毕业典礼演讲多少次，您仍然会看到它并决定不这样做。

sentences.en: I'm not quite sure why you decide not to do it.
sentences.zh: 我不太清楚你为什么决定不这样做。

sentences.en: You're too lazy to do it. It's too hard.
sentences.zh: 你太懒了，做不到。太难了。

sentences.en: You're afraid if you look for your passion and don't find it, you'll feel like you're an idiot, so then you make excuses about why you're not going to look for your passion.
sentences.zh: 你害怕如果你寻找你的激情却找不到它，你会觉得自己是个白痴，所以你会找借口为什么你不去寻找你的激情。

sentences.en: They are excuses, ladies and gentlemen. We're going to go through a whole long list -- your creativity in thinking of excuses not to do what you really need to do if you want to have a great career.
sentences.zh: 女士们先生们，这些都是借口。我们将列出一长串清单——如果你想拥有一份伟大的职业生涯，你在想出不做你真正需要做的事情的借口时的创造力。

sentences.en: So, for example, one of your great excuses is: (Sigh) "Well, great careers are really and truly, for most people, just a matter of luck.
sentences.zh: 因此，举例来说，你最好的借口之一是：（叹气）“好吧，对于大多数人来说，伟大的职业确实只是运气问题。

sentences.en: So I'm going to stand around, I'm going to try to be lucky, and if I'm lucky, I'll have a great career.
sentences.zh: 所以我会袖手旁观，我会努力保持幸运，如果我幸运的话，我将拥有一个伟大的职业生涯。

sentences.en: If not, I'll have a good career." But a good career is an impossibility, so that's not going to work.
sentences.zh: 如果没有的话，我会有一个很好的职业生涯。”但好的职业是不可能的，所以这是行不通的。

sentences.en: Then, your other excuse is, "Yes, there are special people who pursue their passions, but they are geniuses.
sentences.zh: 然后，你的另一个借口是，“是的，有些特殊的人追求他们的激情，但他们是天才。

sentences.en: They are Steven J. I'm not a genius. When I was five, I thought I was a genius, but my professors have beaten that idea out of my head long since."
sentences.zh: 他们是史蒂文·J。我不是天才。当我五岁的时候，我以为自己是个天才，但我的教授们早已把这个想法从我的脑海中抹去了。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "And now I know I am completely competent."
sentences.zh: （笑声）“现在我知道我完全有能力了。”

sentences.en: Now, you see, if this was 1950, being completely competent -- that would have given you a great career.
sentences.zh: 现在，你看，如果这是 1950 年，完全有能力——那会给你一个伟大的职业生涯。

sentences.en: But guess what? This is almost 2012, and saying to the world, "I am totally, completely competent," is damning yourself with the faintest of praise.
sentences.zh: 但是,你猜怎么着?这几乎是2012年, 并且对全世界说, “我完全,完全胜任,” 是在用最微弱的赞美来诅咒你自己。

sentences.en: And then, of course, another excuse: "Well, I would do this, I would do this, but, but -- well, after all, I'm not weird.
sentences.zh: 然后,当然,另一个借口: “嗯,我会这样做,我会这样做,但是—— 毕竟,我不奇怪。

sentences.en: Everybody knows that people who pursue their passions are somewhat obsessive.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道,追求其激情的人有些痴迷。

sentences.en: A little strange. Hmm? OK? You know, a fine line between madness and genius.
sentences.zh: 有点奇怪 知道吗 疯狂和天才之间的界线

sentences.en: "I'm not weird. I've read Steven J.'s biography.
sentences.zh: "我不奇怪,我读过史蒂芬·J的传记"

sentences.en: Oh my goodness -- I'm not that person. I am nice.
sentences.zh: 哦,我的天啊,我不是那个人,我很好

sentences.en: I am normal. I'm a nice, normal person, and nice, normal people -- don't have passion."
sentences.zh: 我是正常人,我是一个善良的正常人, 和善良的正常人--没有激情。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) "Ah, but I still want a great career.
sentences.zh: (笑)"啊,但我仍然 想要一个伟大的职业生涯。

sentences.en: I'm not prepared to pursue my passion, so I know what I'm going to do, because I have a solution.
sentences.zh: 我不准备追求我的激情, 所以我知道我该怎么办, 因为我有一个解决方案。

sentences.en: I have a strategy. It's the one Mommy and Daddy told me about.
sentences.zh: 我有策略,是爸爸妈妈告诉我的

sentences.en: Mommy and Daddy told me that if I worked hard, I'd have a good career.
sentences.zh: 妈妈和爸爸告诉我,如果我努力工作, 我会有一个好的职业生涯。

sentences.en: So, if you work hard and have a good career, if you work really, really hard, you'll have a great career.
sentences.zh: 所以,如果你努力工作 并有一个良好的职业生涯, 如果你真的,真的努力工作, 你会有一个伟大的事业。

sentences.en: Doesn't that, like, mathematically make sense?"
sentences.zh: 这在数学上不合理吗?"

sentences.en: Hmm. Not. But you've managed to talk yourself into that.
sentences.zh: 嗯,没有,但你已经 设法说服自己。

sentences.en: You know what? Here's a little secret: You want to work? You want to work really, really hard?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗,这里有个小秘密:你想工作吗?你真的想工作吗?

sentences.en: You know what? You'll succeed. The world will give you the opportunity to work really, really hard.
sentences.zh: 你会成功的,世界会给你一个真正、非常努力的工作机会

sentences.en: But, are you so sure that that's going to give you a great career, when all the evidence is to the contrary?
sentences.zh: 但是,你这么肯定 这将给你一个伟大的职业生涯, 当所有的证据是相反的?

sentences.en: So let's deal with those of you who are trying to find your passion.
sentences.zh: 让我们来对付你们中那些 试图找到激情的人

sentences.en: You actually understand that you really had better do it, never mind the excuses.
sentences.zh: 你其实明白,你真的有 更好的做到这一点, 不介意的借口。

sentences.en: You're trying to find your passion -- (Sigh) and you're so happy.
sentences.zh: 你试图找到自己的激情 - (叹气) 你是如此的快乐。

sentences.en: You found something you're interested in.
sentences.zh: 你发现了你感兴趣的东西

sentences.en: "I have an interest! I have an interest!"
sentences.zh: "我有兴趣,我有兴趣!"

sentences.en: You tell me. You say, "I have an interest!" I say, "That's wonderful!
sentences.zh: 你说"我有兴趣" 我说"太好了!"

sentences.en: And what are you trying to tell me?" "Well, I have an interest."
sentences.zh: 你想告诉我什么?" "我有兴趣"

sentences.en: I say, "Do you have passion?" "I have an interest," you say.
sentences.zh: 我说:"你有激情吗?" 你说:"我有兴趣"

sentences.en: "Your interest is compared to what?" "Well, I'm interested in this."
sentences.zh: “你的兴趣与什么相比？” “嗯，我对这个很感兴趣。”

sentences.en: "And what about the rest of humanity's activities?"
sentences.zh: “那么人类的其他活动呢？”

sentences.en: "I'm not interested in them." "You've looked at them all, have you?"
sentences.zh: “我对他们不感兴趣。” “你都看过了，是吗？”

sentences.en: "No. Not exactly." Passion is your greatest love.
sentences.zh: “不。不完全是。”激情是你最大的爱。

sentences.en: Passion is the thing that will help you create the highest expression of your talent.
sentences.zh: 激情能够帮助你最大限度地发挥你的才能。

sentences.en: Passion, interest -- it's not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 热情、兴趣——这不是一回事。

sentences.en: Are you really going to go to your sweetie and say, "Marry me! You're interesting."
sentences.zh: 你真的要去找你的爱人说：“嫁给我吧！你很有趣。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Won't happen. Won't happen, and you will die alone.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 不会发生的。不会发生的，你会孤独地死去。

sentences.en: (Laughter) What you want, what you want, what you want, is passion.
sentences.zh: （笑声）你想要的，你想要的，你想要的，就是激情。

sentences.en: It is beyond interest. You need 20 interests, and then one of them, one of them might grab you, one of them might engage you more than anything else, and then you may have found your greatest love,
sentences.zh: 这是超出兴趣的。你需要20个兴趣，然后其中一个，其中一个可能会抓住你，其中一个可能比其他任何事情都更吸引你，然后你可能找到了你最大的爱，

sentences.en: in comparison to all the other things that interest you, and that's what passion is.
sentences.zh: 与所有其他你感兴趣的事情相比，这就是激情。

sentences.en: I have a friend, proposed to his sweetie.
sentences.zh: 我有一个朋友，向他的心上人求婚了。

sentences.en: He was an economically rational person. He said to his sweetie, "Let us marry.
sentences.zh: 他是一个经济上理性的人。他对他的爱人说：“我们结婚吧。

sentences.en: Let us merge our interests." (Laughter) Yes, he did.
sentences.zh: 让我们融合我们的利益。” （笑声） 是的，他做到了。

sentences.en: "I love you truly," he said. "I love you deeply.
sentences.zh: “我真的爱你，”他说。 “我深深地爱着你。

sentences.en: I love you more than any other woman I've ever encountered.
sentences.zh: 我比我遇到过的任何其他女人都更爱你。

sentences.en: I love you more than Mary, Jane, Susie, Penelope, Ingrid, Gertrude, Gretel -- I was on a German exchange program then.
sentences.zh: 我爱你们胜过玛丽、简、苏西、佩内洛普、英格丽德、格特鲁德、格蕾特——当时我正在参加一个德国交换项目。

sentences.en: I love you more than --" All right. She left the room halfway through his enumeration of his love for her.
sentences.zh: 我爱你胜过——”好吧。当他列举对她的爱时，她中途离开了房间。

sentences.en: After he got over his surprise at being, you know, turned down, he concluded he'd had a narrow escape from marrying an irrational person.
sentences.zh: 当他克服了被拒绝的惊讶之后，他得出结论，他侥幸逃脱了嫁给一个非理性的人的命运。

sentences.en: Although, he did make a note to himself that the next time he proposed, it was perhaps not necessary to enumerate all of the women he had auditioned for the part.
sentences.zh: 不过，他确实提醒自己，下次求婚时，也许没有必要一一列举他试镜过的所有女性。

sentences.en: (Laughter) But the point stands. You must look for alternatives so that you find your destiny, or are you afraid of the word "destiny"?
sentences.zh: （笑声）但这一点是正确的。你必须寻找替代方案，以便找到你的命运，或者你害怕“命运”这个词吗？

sentences.en: Does the word "destiny" scare you? That's what we're talking about.
sentences.zh: “命运”这个词让你害怕吗？这就是我们正在谈论的。

sentences.en: And if you don't find the highest expression of your talent, if you settle for "interesting," what the hell ever that means, do you know what will happen at the end of your long life?
sentences.zh: 如果你找不到自己才能的最高表达，如果你满足于“有趣”，那到底意味着什么，你知道在你漫长的一生结束时会发生什么吗？

sentences.en: Your friends and family will be gathered in the cemetery, and there beside your gravesite will be a tombstone, and inscribed on that tombstone it will say, "Here lies a distinguished engineer,
sentences.zh: 你的朋友和家人将聚集在墓地，你的墓地旁边将有一块墓碑，墓碑上刻着这样的字：“这里长眠着一位杰出的工程师，

sentences.en: who invented Velcro." But what that tombstone should have said, in an alternative lifetime, what it should have said if it was your highest expression of talent,
sentences.zh: 谁发明了魔术贴。”但是，在另一个人生中，那块墓碑应该写什么，如果这是你才华的最高表达，它应该写什么，

sentences.en: was, "Here lies the last Nobel Laureate in Physics, who formulated the Grand Unified Field Theory and demonstrated the practicality of warp drive."
sentences.zh: 是，“这里长眠着最后一位诺贝尔物理学奖获得者，他提出了大统一场论并证明了曲速驱动的实用性。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Velcro, indeed! (Laughter) One was a great career.
sentences.zh: （笑声）魔术贴，确实如此！ （笑声） 其中一个是一项伟大的职业。

sentences.en: One was a missed opportunity. But then, there are some of you who, in spite of all these excuses, you will find, you will find your passion.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是错失了机会。但是，你们中的一些人，尽管有所有这些借口，你会发现，你会找到你的激情。

sentences.en: And you'll still fail. You're going to fail, because -- because you're not going to do it, because you will have invented a new excuse,
sentences.zh: 而你仍然会失败。你将会失败，因为——因为你不会这么做，因为你会发明一个新的借口，

sentences.en: any excuse to fail to take action, and this excuse, I've heard so many times: "Yes, I would pursue a great career,
sentences.zh: 任何不采取行动的借口，这个借口，我听过很多次：“是的，我会追求伟大的职业，

sentences.en: but, I value human relationships -- (Laughter) more than accomplishment.
sentences.zh: 但是，我更看重人际关系——（笑声）胜过成就。

sentences.en: I want to be a great friend. I want to be a great spouse.
sentences.zh: 我想成为一个好朋友。我想成为一个伟大的配偶。

sentences.en: I want to be a great parent, and I will not sacrifice them on the altar of great accomplishment."
sentences.zh: 我想成为一名伟大的父母，我不会在伟大成就的祭坛上牺牲他们。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) What do you want me to say? Now, do you really want me to say now, tell you, "Really, I swear I don't kick children."
sentences.zh: （笑声）你想让我说什么？现在，你真的想让我现在说，告诉你，“真的，我发誓我不踢孩子。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) Look at the worldview you've given yourself.
sentences.zh: （笑声）看看你给自己设定的世界观。

sentences.en: You're a hero no matter what. And I, by suggesting ever so delicately that you might want a great career, must hate children.
sentences.zh: 无论如何你都是英雄。我如此微妙地暗示你可能想要一份伟大的职业，但我一定讨厌孩子。

sentences.en: I don't hate children. I don't kick them.
sentences.zh: 我不讨厌孩子。我不踢他们。

sentences.en: Yes, there was a little kid wandering through this building when I came here, and no, I didn't kick him.
sentences.zh: 是的，当我来到这里时，有一个小孩在这栋大楼里徘徊，不，我没有踢他。

sentences.en: (Laughter) Course, I had to tell him the building was for adults only, and to get out.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 当然，我必须告诉他这栋大楼仅供成人使用，然后离开。

sentences.en: He mumbled something about his mother, and I told him she'd probably find him outside anyway.
sentences.zh: 他咕哝了一些关于他母亲的事情，我告诉他无论如何她可能会在外面找到他。

sentences.en: Last time I saw him, he was on the stairs crying.
sentences.zh: 上次我见到他时，他正在楼梯上哭泣。

sentences.en: (Laughter) What a wimp. (Laughter) But what do you mean? That's what you expect me to say.
sentences.zh: （笑声）真是个懦夫。 （笑声）但是你的意思是什么？这就是你期望我说的话。

sentences.en: Do you really think it's appropriate that you should actually take children and use them as a shield?
sentences.zh: 你真的认为你应该把孩子当作盾牌吗？

sentences.en: You know what will happen someday, you ideal parent, you?
sentences.zh: 你知道有一天会发生什么，你理想的父母，你吗？

sentences.en: The kid will come to you someday and say, "I know what I want to be.
sentences.zh: 有一天，孩子会来找你说：“我知道我想成为什么。

sentences.en: I know what I'm going to do with my life."
sentences.zh: 我知道我这一生要做什么。”

sentences.en: You are so happy. It's the conversation a parent wants to hear, because your kid's good in math, and you know you're going to like what comes next.
sentences.zh: 你真幸福。这是家长想听到的对话，因为你的孩子数学很好，而且你知道你会喜欢接下来发生的事情。

sentences.en: Says your kid, "I have decided I want to be a magician.
sentences.zh: 你的孩子说：“我决定要成为一名魔术师。

sentences.en: I want to perform magic tricks on the stage."
sentences.zh: 我想在舞台上表演魔术。”

sentences.en: (Laughter) And what do you say? You say, you say, "That's risky, kid.
sentences.zh: （笑声） 你说什么？你说，你说，“这很危险，孩子。

sentences.en: Might fail, kid. Don't make a lot of money at that, kid.
sentences.zh: 可能会失败，孩子。孩子，别靠这个赚很多钱。

sentences.en: I don't know, kid, you should think about that again, kid.
sentences.zh: 我不知道，孩子，你应该再考虑一下，孩子。

sentences.en: You're so good at math, why don't you --" The kid interrupts you and says, "But it is my dream. It is my dream to do this."
sentences.zh: 你数学这么好，为什么不——”孩子打断你的话，说道，“但这是我的梦想。做到这一点是我的梦想。”

sentences.en: And what are you going to say? You know what you're going to say?
sentences.zh: 你要说什么？你知道你要说什么吗？

sentences.en: "Look kid. I had a dream once, too, but -- But --" So how are you going to finish the sentence with your "but"?
sentences.zh: “看孩子。我也曾经做过一个梦，但是——但是——”那么你要如何用“但是”来结束这句话呢？

sentences.en: "But. I had a dream too, once, kid, but I was afraid to pursue it."
sentences.zh: “但是。我曾经也有过一个梦想，孩子，但我不敢去追求它。”

sentences.en: Or are you going to tell him this: "I had a dream once, kid.
sentences.zh: 或者你会告诉他：“我曾经做过一个梦，孩子。

sentences.en: But then, you were born." (Laughter) (Applause) Do you really want to use your family, do you really ever want to look at your spouse and your kid,
sentences.zh: 但后来，你出生了。”（笑声）（掌声）你真的想利用你的家庭吗？你真的想看看你的配偶和孩子吗？

sentences.en: and see your jailers? There was something you could have said to your kid, when he or she said, "I have a dream."
sentences.zh: 看看你的狱卒？当你的孩子说“我有一个梦想”时，你可以对他或她说一些话。

sentences.en: You could have said -- looked the kid in the face and said, "Go for it, kid!
sentences.zh: 你可以说——看着孩子的脸说：“加油，孩子！

sentences.en: Just like I did." But you won't be able to say that, because you didn't.
sentences.zh: 就像我一样。”但你不能这么说，因为你没有。

sentences.en: So you can't. (Laughter) And so the sins of the parents are visited on the poor children.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能。 （笑声）所以父母的罪孽就降临到了可怜的孩子身上。

sentences.en: Why will you seek refuge in human relationships as your excuse not to find and pursue your passion?
sentences.zh: 为什么你会在人际关系中寻求庇护作为你不去寻找和追求你的激情的借口？

sentences.en: You know why. In your heart of hearts, you know why, and I'm being deadly serious.
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么。在你们内心深处，你们知道为什么，而且我是非常认真的。

sentences.en: You know why you would get all warm and fuzzy and wrap yourself up in human relationships.
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么你会变得温暖而模糊，并把自己包裹在人际关系中。

sentences.en: It is because you are -- you know what you are.
sentences.zh: 这是因为你——你知道你是什么。

sentences.en: You're afraid to pursue your passion. You're afraid to look ridiculous.
sentences.zh: 你害怕追求你的激情。你害怕看起来很可笑。

sentences.en: You're afraid to try. You're afraid you may fail.
sentences.zh: 你害怕尝试。你害怕你可能会失败。

sentences.en: Great friend, great spouse, great parent, great career.
sentences.zh: 伟大的朋友，伟大的配偶，伟大的父母，伟大的事业。

sentences.en: Is that not a package? Is that not who you are?
sentences.zh: 那不是一个包裹吗？那不是你吗？

sentences.en: How can you be one without the other? But you're afraid.
sentences.zh: 你们怎么能成为一个没有另一个的人呢？但你害怕了。

sentences.en: And that's why you're not going to have a great career.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么你不会有一个伟大的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Unless -- "unless," that most evocative of all English words -- "unless."
sentences.zh: 除非——“除非”，这是所有英语单词中最能唤起人们回忆的——“除非”。

sentences.en: But the "unless" word is also attached to that other, most terrifying phrase, "If only I had ..."
sentences.zh: 但是“除非”这个词也附加在另一个最可怕的短语上，“如果我有......”

sentences.en: "If only I had ..." If you ever have that thought ricocheting in your brain, it will hurt a lot.
sentences.zh: “要是我……就好了”如果你的脑子里曾经有过这样的想法，那会很痛苦。

sentences.en: So, those are the many reasons why you are going to fail to have a great career.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些就是你无法拥有伟大职业生涯的众多原因。

sentences.en: Unless -- Unless. Thank you. (Applause)
sentences.zh: 除非——除非。谢谢。 （掌声）
